rv.q: It is hard to feel the intimacy of lovers when they are being whisked from bollard to bollard.
Watching the stage version is like seeing a Technicolor film rendered in black and white...
Here, though, they impose similar techniques on a fragile story that can't survive them.
It's all rather insipid and bitty - the film's colour is lost, and little is added.
I have to say that the film is far from being my own tasse de tisane, with its Gallic artiness and a whimsical charm that often borders on the downright kitsch.
The approach here is quieter, more low-tech and – if they can do something about that first “mauvais quart d’heure” – just as seductive.
